rubrics.justification: The response overstates image-based certainty. The blastocoel does not clearly occupy most of the embryo, the ICM is not distinctly well-defined in this image, and TE uniformity/cohesiveness is difficult to confirm visually. It relies heavily on the provided Gardner grade rather than the visible morphology.
It thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, tubal factor diagnosis, sperm parameters, endometrium, cycle history, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with probability estimates broadly matching the clinical picture. Minor issues include somewhat speculative quantitative adjustments and double-counting concerns around morphology/euploidy and fresh-transfer effects.

Recommendations are largely consistent with standard IVF practice, especially support for single embryo transfer. Small deviations include speculative suggestions such as routine estradiol addition, progesterone target checking, and ERA consideration after only limited failure history.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer management and future planning, including SET, luteal support, follow-up, and contingency planning. Some recommendations are more center-specific than universally indicated.
